subject: Pilot extension + limited-time incentive structure for Aether Systems
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@aethersys.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aethersys.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway & incentive question

Hi Diego,

Quick note from our side after the last demo — the engineering team wants another 3 weeks to validate inference latency at peak load. We have about 40% of the original token budget left, but we need more time to run the longer scenarios (and one more model variant).

Two asks: can Redwood extend the pilot by 21 days, and can you provide a limited, one-time incentive (either credits or a short-term price uplift for seats) to cover the extra capacity? Procurement would like an approach that keeps our finance team comfortable (clear offsets or invoice credits).

We’re under a tight procurement cadence and would need an amendment by next week if possible.

Appreciate any options you can share — we’d rather not re-spin a new POC if we can patch the current one.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director, AI Engineering
Aether Systems

Attachments: aether-pilot-usage-summary.csv (usage export)
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@aethersys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot runway & incentive question

Hi Julia — thanks for the heads up and for the usage export (helpful).

We can absolutely avoid re-provisioning a fresh pilot. Two pragmatic options we typically use:

1) Time extension + small top-up credits: extend the existing timebox by 21 days and add a flat credit equal to the expected marginal GPU hours (we usually price this as a % of the remaining usage). This keeps your invoice simple — we show a single amendment credit line.

2) Short-term seat uplift: add a temporary seat/throughput uplift for the 21-day window at a discounted uplift rate (lower than list) so you pay only for the uplift you consume. This is cleaner if you expect bursty peaks.

Both can be documented as a 1-page amendment. If procurement needs invoicing offsets, option 1 maps to a credit memo; option 2 maps to prorated invoice lines.

I’ve attached a short PDF with model numbers and rough pricing buckets so you can share with procurement. If you’re okay, I’ll loop in Marissa (Finance) to confirm the credit memo flow and Olga (CS) for the onboarding checklist for the extra model.

Which option would procurement prefer? If you want, we can do a brief 20-min sync early next week and I’ll bring the pricing scenarios.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pilot-incentive-options.pdf
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Julia Park <julia@aethersys.com>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot runway & incentive question

Hi Julia — looping finance in. Quick notes on flow so procurement can map to internal processes: 

- Option 1 (extension + credit memo): We issue an amendment that lists the 21-day extension and the credit line (nominal $X equal to estimated GPU-hour cost). The credit will appear on the next invoice as a negative line item; if you need a standalone credit memo PDF, we can generate that.

- Option 2 (seat uplift): We will add a temporary SKU for the uplifted throughput. That SKU will be prorated for the 21 days and invoiced as normal. If Aether requires a discount code or PO-based line item, we can include the SKU and the discounted rate in the amendment.

We prefer option 1 for speed (single amendment, simple accounting) but happy to support whichever procurement prefers. I’ll prepare the amendment draft and the credit memo template — Diego, want me to send the draft to Julia and procurement after lunch?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)
From: Julia Park <julia@aethersys.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aethersys.com, olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway & incentive question

Thanks Marissa — procurement is aligned to Option 1 (extension + credit memo). Two requests from our side:

- Can the credit be documented as a separate credit memo PDF (our AP team requires an auditable credit document)
- Can the amendment explicitly call out that the extension does not alter data retention or SLA commitments (we’re running in Redwood Hosted and legal likes that spelled out)

If you can push the draft amendment + credit memo PDF by end of day Wednesday Pacific, we’ll route through procurement and sign. If possible, include a single DocuSign link for the amendment to keep signatures clean.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’d like to keep momentum on the evaluation.

— Julia
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@aethersys.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>, procurement@aethersys.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot runway & incentive question

Perfect — we’ll do Option 1 and include the two items you asked for. Plan:

1) Marissa will generate the amendment + credit memo PDF and route a DocuSign link (I’ll ask legal to add the short clause explicitly excluding changes to data retention and SLAs).
2) Olga will confirm onboarding checklist for the additional model variant and confirm any tagging needed on the trial instance.
3) I’ll send a HubSpot update with the amendment and set a 21-day reminder to check progress.

Target: amendment + DocuSign link to Julia & procurement by EOD Wednesday (Pacific). If procurement has special PO line requirements, send them back in one reply and we’ll include them in the amendment.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping the evaluation live.
